I have been working this land for fifty years. Quzhou soil I know well — the loam holds moisture when I irrigate right, and the winters here mean wheat always comes first. My 10.1 mu is not big but it feeds my household and gives me something to sell. Two people do not need much, but I still want good yields. I cannot afford to gamble.

For wheat, I plant in October as always. I will buy improved certified seed from the township supply store — Jimai or Kenong variety, whichever they have that resists rust. I stopped using saved seed years ago; the yields are not the same. I put down compound fertilizer before plowing, then top-dress urea at jointing. I rotary-till the maize stubble under before sowing — it breaks up the stalks and keeps the soil loose. I irrigate four times: once before winter sets in to help the roots, once at jointing, once at heading, and once at grain filling if it looks dry. I spray herbicide in late winter when the weeds come up, then fungicide and one more pesticide around heading. Should get around 450 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

After wheat harvest in June I plant maize right away — no wasting time. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, because that is just what you do now. No tilling — I drill straight into the stubble. Saves my back at my age too. I apply fertilizer in two goes: some compound at planting, then urea when the plants are knee-high. Maize in summer here gets the July rains usually, so I only irrigate twice — once if the ground is too dry at planting, and once at tasseling if there is a drought. One pesticide pass for aphids and corn borer is usually enough. I expect around 550 jin per mu.
